intro.text: A bridgeman in Bridge Four who openly resists Kaladin's early efforts to lead the crew.
A former bridgeman and lieutenant of Bridge Four, chosen with Skar to guard Dalinar Kholin as one of the crew's best fighters.
A former member of Bridge Four and a Shardbearer who fled the warcamps after a failed plot to kill King Elhokar.
A former bridgeman who joined the Fused, killed King Elhokar, and took the singer name Vyre along with an Honorblade.

story.text: When Kaladin began trying to reform Bridge Four, he made an example of Moash, hauling him out of bed and carrying him outside. Annoyed, Moash asked Gaz whether they had to obey Kaladin, and when told no, the bridgemen dispersed.

During chasm duty, Moash mocked Kaladin as a "lordling" and spread Gaz's claim that Kaladin had lied about being a squadleader, until Kaladin's spear kata stunned everyone into silence. Moash accepted Rock's stew that night but still refused to train the next morning.

Kaladin made Moash a subsquad commander alongside Rock, Teft and Skar, explaining that his stubborn resistance showed a strong will. Moash said he still didn't trust Kaladin, but was curious enough to follow.
After Kaladin was beaten and strung up for the side carry maneuver, Moash joined Teft and Rock in promising to remember him, acknowledging that Kaladin had done it to save them.

Moash told Kaladin he had hoped to win a Shardblade when he came to war. Unlike Kaladin, he said he would join the lighteyes if given the chance, and planned to use a Blade to change the world so others would not suffer abuse.

Moash took eagerly to spear training, learning faster than nearly anyone. When Dunny died on a bridge run, Moash knocked Kaladin down to keep him from running out after the body, likely saving his life. Afterward, Moash admitted he had been wrong about Kaladin, and they shook hands.

Now trusting Kaladin, Moash defended him to the others and begged to keep an emerald broam found in the chasms, offering to swallow it. He stood with Kaladin as soldiers pelted the crew with fruit, and led Bridge Four in their first salute to him.

Exhausted by extra duties, Moash proposed charging Sadeas and taking some lighteyes with them, but Kaladin had another plan: wearing armor of Parshendi carapace to draw arrows. It worked, and Moash was thrilled.
Moash trained relentlessly, telling Kaladin he sought vengeance but not against whom. He said Kaladin had kept his plans alive and swore to guard him with his life.

In the assault on the Tower, Moash was one of the decoys wearing carapace armor, and carried the wounded Teft to Kaladin. He watched with Kaladin as Sadeas retreated unharmed, then agreed with the crew to go back and help Dalinar's army.

When Kaladin collapsed from exhaustion, Moash took command and got the bridge back into place, then led the defense against Parshendi who leapt the chasm. He followed Kaladin to Adolin Kholin and reluctantly retreated with Adolin at Kaladin's order.
After Dalinar traded his Shardblade for the bridgemen, Moash celebrated with the crew in the Kholin warcamp and was eager to learn Kaladin's powers.

Moash stayed on as Dalinar's bodyguard, made a lieutenant and chosen with Skar to guard Dalinar. Skeptical of Dalinar, he still hoped to learn the sword. Having no slave brand, he alone took his Bridge Four tattoo on his upper arm.

Moash nearly picked a fight with a lighteyed gate guard who doubted Kaladin, but apologized after Kaladin rebuked him. Guarding Adolin and Renarin, he asked about Amaram, and learned Amaram had branded Kaladin; they agreed to someday get back at the lighteyes who had wronged them.

After an attempt on the king's life, Kaladin learned Moash had lingered on the balcony after his shift, but dismissed suspicion. When Szeth attacked during a highstorm, Moash guarded the rear and hauled Renarin to safety.
When Sigzil's theory about a smuggled rope pointed toward Moash, Kaladin tried to question him, but Moash only asked what they would do about Amaram and urged Kaladin to come out drinking.
Kaladin brought Moash to train with a Shardblade under Zahel and Ivis. Moash eagerly grabbed the Blade first and kept practicing through breaks.

Moash told Kaladin that Elhokar had thrown his grandparents, Ana and Da, into prison, where they died while he was away with a caravan. Kaladin confronted him about the balcony railing, and Moash agreed to pause his plans if Kaladin would hear out a man named Graves.

Moash had been recruited by Graves through Rill, an old caravan acquaintance. At a tavern, he brought Kaladin to meet Graves's group, who called themselves patriots and wanted Dalinar as king. Afterward Kaladin refused to betray his duty and forbade Moash from meeting them again.

When Adolin offered Kaladin a Shardblade and Shardplate, Kaladin gave them to Moash, raising him to lighteyed rank. Moash repainted the Plate blue and red, and his eyes began to lighten within a week.
Moash joined Graves in an attempt to kill King Elhokar, which Kaladin thwarted. Moash fled the warcamps with Graves, taking his Shards.
As a slave of the Fused, Moash hauled supply sledges. He stood up for singers forced to pull sledges, earning respect, and joined the assault on Kholinar as a warrior.
After Moash killed one of the Fused, the others offered him a choice: give up his weapons and go with them, or die. The Fused he had slain, Leshwi, did not seek revenge, admiring his passion instead.
In Kholinar, Moash fought the Wall Guard and reached King Elhokar, stabbing him to death as the king tried to swear the First Ideal. He saluted the stunned Kaladin and left.

Guilt at Kaladin's reaction led Moash to let Odium take away his pain. A Fused sent him to kill the Herald Jezrien with a special knife. Leshwi then offered him Jezrien's Honorblade and a new identity, and he took the singer name Vyre and flew with the Fused.

In the assault on Hearthstone, Moash killed Roshone in front of Kaladin and urged the shocked Kaladin to kill himself. Renarin stopped him with a vision of the Windrunner Moash could have become, and Moash fled.
In Kholinar, Moash warned the Nine that Kaladin would foil their plan to occupy Urithiru. Afterward, Odium came to him and asked how best to torment Kaladin.

During the occupation of Urithiru, Moash operated the Oathgate for the Fused. He set a trap for Kaladin in his family's clinic, but Teft and Lift sprang it. Moash wounded Lift, destroyed Teft's spren with an anti-Stormlight dagger, and killed Teft. He handed Lirin to the Fused to be killed if Kaladin fought.

Moash nearly killed Navani before she bonded the tower's spren, whose Light forced his pain back onto him. Hating himself over Teft, he fled, broke his spine in a fall, and was rescued by Heavenly Ones, but woke blind.

Odium and a Fused drove crystal spikes into Moash's empty eye sockets, letting him see Investiture as outlines of light, including living things, gems and spren, but not color. Asked if he was ready to serve, he said he would do what must be done.

Moash arrived on the Shattered Plains with enemy reinforcements. When Leyten's squad found him, a fabrial he carried cut off their Radiant powers, and Sigzil was caught too when he came to help; Moash's Honorblade still worked.

Sigzil tried to keep Moash talking, and Moash accused him of choosing the lighteyes over him. Able to see spren, Moash struck suddenly, killing Leyten's spren with his anti-Stormlight dagger and then stabbing Leyten, before giving a Bridge Four salute and withdrawing.

Moash wounded Sigzil's spren, but Sigzil renounced his oaths before the killing blow, turning her into a Blade he used to fend Moash off. Lopen tackled Moash and broke the fabrial, and with Bridge Four arriving, Moash retreated.

personality.text: Moash is strong-willed and slow to trust, at first resisting Kaladin loudly. Once won over, he trains with fierce dedication, driven by a desire for vengeance he keeps to himself.

Moash is standoffish and grim with strangers but attaches quickly once he warms to someone, often leading off-duty fun. He values his friends, admires power and wants it, yet distrusts those above him. His strong sense of justice stems from what happened to his grandparents.

His need for vengeance against Elhokar, and then all lighteyes, consumes Moash and pulls him away from his friends toward the enemy. After giving in to Odium, he tells himself he feels nothing as he follows the Fused.

Moash is a tall, lean but strong young Alethi with a narrow, hawkish face, a prominent nose, a scarred chin and brown hair flecked with black. Born darkeyed, his eyes lighten after he gains Shards, and they glow blue when he uses an Honorblade.

As Vyre, Kaladin is the one person who brings back Moash's painful emotions. He becomes fixated on making Kaladin admit Moash was right, believing that pushing him to suicide would be a mercy, though he will not kill Kaladin himself.
